meta.title: Solutions — Financial, Operational & Supply Chain Intelligence
meta.description: Financial intelligence, operational analytics, supply chain analysis, accounting intelligence, advisory and managed services. Six capabilities that work as one engagement.

hero.title: Six capabilities. One engagement.
hero.subtitle: Companies rarely have a purely financial problem or a purely operational one. Forcelis is organized so the analysis crosses those lines the way the business does.

groups.title: Financial Intelligence
groups.lead: Understand what the company earns, what it spends, where the margin is created and where it is lost.
groups.outcome: A management view of the business that reconciles with accounting, updates every period, and answers the question the P&L does not: which part of the business is actually paying for the rest.

groups.title: Operational Intelligence
groups.lead: Find where process, not price, is costing money — and quantify it before anyone is asked to change how they work.
groups.outcome: A prioritized list of inefficiencies with an estimated annual cost attached to each, so the effort of fixing them can be compared against the return.

groups.title: Supply Chain Intelligence
groups.lead: Inventory, purchasing, suppliers and payment terms are one system. Analyzed separately, each looks fine.
groups.outcome: A clear read on how much cash the operation is holding, where it is held, and which supplier or product line is responsible for the change.

groups.title: Accounting Intelligence
groups.lead: Accounting data is the most complete record most companies have. It is also the least used for decisions.
groups.outcome: Fiscal and accounting information restated in managerial terms — comparable across periods, with data quality issues surfaced rather than silently absorbed into the totals.

groups.title: Business Advisory
groups.lead: Analysis that stops at the finding is unfinished work. This is where it becomes a decision.
groups.outcome: A short set of decisions with an owner, a sequence and a measure — reviewed against the numbers in the following period rather than filed.

groups.title: Managed Services
groups.lead: Once a process is defined and working, someone has to run it every month. That can be Forcelis.
groups.outcome: A managed capability with defined scope, methodology and reporting — under Forcelis quality control and a single point of accountability.

note.title: How engagements usually start
note.body: Most clients begin with a Business Diagnostic. It establishes the baseline, shows which of these capabilities the company actually needs, and makes the scope of anything that follows a matter of evidence rather than a proposal.

closing.title: Not sure which of these you need?
closing.body: That is what the diagnostic is for. It starts from your data, not from a service catalogue.
